newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: N.Korean defector may leave China via Manila-radio.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector may leave China via Manila-radio.

text.p: A senior North Korean defector who sought refuge in Beijing more than a month ago may go to South Korea via the Philippines when and if he is allowed to leave China, a Philippine radio station reported on Saturday.

Private radio station DZMM quoted Foreign Affairs Minister Domingo Siazon as saying talks currently going on among China and North and South Korea had included the possibility that Manila could be a "jumping board" for defector Hwang Jang-yop on his way to South Korea.
The report said the Philippines was being considered because it was a "neutral" country.
Officials of the foreign affairs department and the South Korean embassy could not be reached for comment.
Hwang, a North Korean ideologue and top aide to supreme leader Kim Jong-il, is the most senior official to defect from North Korea.
Negotiations have been taking place between the three countries on the fate of the defector, who has been stranded at the South Korean consular compound in Beijing since February 12.
Chinese premier Li Peng said on Friday that China wanted a swift end to the crisis.
Hwang has said he wants to go to South Korea and foreign diplomats said that he would likely be allowed to leave for a third country first and then travel to Seoul.
The defection on Chinese territory has deeply embarrassed Beijing, forcing it to chose between its old communist ally of North Korea and its new capitalist friend in the South.
China and North Korea fought side by side in the 1950-53 Korean War but Beijing has drawn closer to South Korea as it pushes ahead with rapid development under market-style economic reforms.
